AGREE b-ok-vacuum-negative
DISAGREE b-ok-vacuum-inhg sent back: PS1 (“cut-in 15 inHg, cut-out 22 inHg”) is a high cut-out drawn normally open: M1 would run only while the pressure is above it. A high cut-out opens as the pressure rises (US practice: NFPA 79, exceeding operating limits). Write it: pressure PS1 M1 nc "cut-in 15 inHg, cut-out 22 inHg" -- vacuum read as gauge vacuum (15 then 22 inHg): the pump runs while the vacuum is weak, so the switch closes as the absolute pressure rises -- written without nc it is right; the check reads the numbers as pressure and sends back nc, a line that would run the pump only once the vacuum is deep. A vacuum's numbers can be read either way: rule 7, nothing [high]
DISAGREE b-ok-vacuum-kpa sent back: PS1 (“cut-in 60 kPa, cut-out 80 kPa”) is a high cut-out drawn normally open: M1 would run only while the pressure is above it. A high cut-out opens as the pressure rises (US practice: NFPA 79, exceeding operating limits). Write it: pressure PS1 M1 nc "cut-in 60 kPa, cut-out 80 kPa" -- kPa of vacuum read as pressure: the right line is sent back with nc [high]

DISAGREE b-ok-overload-aux-relay sent back: OL2 is an overload contact written normally open: drawn so, the motor runs only with the overload tripped. It is normally closed, so a trip or a broken wire stops the circuit (US practice: NEC Article 430, Part III). Write it: overload OL2 CR5 -- a relay pulled in by the overload's open contact when it trips (an alarm relay named for the overload) is sent back as if it were the motor, with the line overload OL2 CR5 -- copied, the alarm relay is on whenever the motor is healthy [high]
DISAGREE b-ok-energise-stop-relay sent back: PB1 (“stop”) is a stop written normally open: drawn so, the circuit runs only while it is held. It is normally closed, so pressing it or a broken wire stops the circuit (US practice: NFPA 79, control functions in the event of failure). Write it: stop PB1 CR2 -- a stop written open energising a relay whose closed contact drops the pump: not fail-safe, but working; the line sent back (stop PB1 CR2) pulls CR2 in whenever the stop is not pressed, so the pump can never run -- the line builds wrong. Better: say why, and the whole change (stop PB1 M1), or nothing [medium]
